title: Cho trẻ tự đi học · Causes / Problems / Solutions
prompt: Some communities are considering allowing older children to travel to school independently. What problems could this create, and how could these problems be addressed?

source.detail: Bài luyện mở rộng biên soạn riêng cho năm 2026. Tham khảo các nhóm chủ đề trong forecast công khai; tình huống, bài mẫu và phân tích được viết mới.
source.disclaimer: Không xác nhận đề này đã xuất hiện hoặc sẽ xuất hiện trong kỳ thi. Các chủ đề ngách được bổ sung để mở rộng phạm vi luyện tập; không gán xác suất ra thi.

keywords: Cho trẻ tự đi học Tự di chuyển có thể giúp trẻ tập định hướng và phán đoán hợp lý khi không có người lớn giám sát bởi vì việc nhiều lần chọn chỗ sang đường an toàn biến luật giao thông trừu tượng thành quyết định có hệ quả trực tiếp. Minh họa: Trẻ có thể đi cùng cha mẹ trước, rồi đi với hàng xóm, trước khi tự đi trên cùng tuyến quen thuộc. Không suy rộng từ ví dụ thành bảo đảm thành công cho tất cả.
instructions: Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words.
paragraphs: Travelling to school without an adult can build practical independence, but children do not encounter equally safe routes or develop judgement at identical ages. The principal concern is clear: an independence policy can expose children to traffic hazards that confidence alone cannot overcome; addressing it requires a response tailored to that harm rather than abandoning the objective automatically.

An independence policy can expose children to traffic hazards that confidence alone cannot overcome. The initial attraction nevertheless needs to be recognised: independent journeys can help children practise navigation and sensible judgement outside adult supervision. This attraction arises because repeatedly choosing a safe crossing turns abstract road rules into decisions with immediate consequences, which explains why the proposal can gain support despite its risks. Repeated journeys let adults check judgement gradually, whereas a sudden withdrawal of supervision reveals weaknesses only after a child encounters difficulty.

Parents and schools should assess crossings and provide a staged transition rather than treating age as the only criterion. A child could first walk with a parent, then with a neighbour, before travelling alone along the same familiar route. The route can be reviewed as traffic patterns change, rather than approved permanently after one successful attempt. A child who can cross a quiet street confidently may still lack the judgement needed at a congested junction where drivers frequently ignore pedestrians and visibility is poor. The response must preserve the central limit: independence is appropriate only where the route and the child’s actual abilities make it reasonably safe.

The principal problems are a mismatch between confidence and ability, and exposure to unsafe roads. Repeated practice, realistic route assessment and gradual withdrawal of supervision address those risks more effectively than either an automatic age threshold or a blanket prohibition on independent travel.

vocabulary.meaning: sự giám sát của người lớn
